headline: Hybrid neural-state-space models of iEEG and few-shot selection of neural latents
label: Neural Dynamics Decoding Models
summary: Recent preprints and a publication extend learned dynamical models to intracranial, fMRI, and latent-variable neural data, with new emphasis on validation.
synthesis: The common thread is temporally structured modeling of neural activity, with predictive performance used as the criterion for model quality. DFINE, a framework coupling neural networks with linear state-space models, is extended to human iEEG recordings, where it is reported to outperform LSSMs. A time-aware graph neural network with transformer fusion models dynamic fMRI connectivity alongside tabular data to forecast future tobacco use. A separate publication proposes few-shot co-smoothing as a secondary metric for latent variable models, intended to select latents that better reflect true dynamics. What is new across these items is attention to how models are selected and validated, not only which architecture is used. The three items differ in modality, scope, and objective, so the shared element is the dynamical modeling framing rather than a common architecture.
